# claude-bughunter

> A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **85 skills** · 16 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com).

Built by **Sachin Sharma** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

 
   SPONSORED BY 
   
   
   
     
       
       
     
   
        
   
     
       
       
     
   
 

---

## What is this?

`claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the Claude Code skills system. Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope.

Four layers stack:

- **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline.
- **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates.
- **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation.
- **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables.

All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name.

---

## Quickstart

**Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls
```

All 85 skills + 16 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`.

**A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them.

git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git
cd Claude-BugHunter
```

# macOS / Linux
bash scripts/install.sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1
```

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

   "大道至简" 
 

 

中文 | English

 

* 此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。
* MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。
* 项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。
* MiniMind 同时拓展了视觉模态模型 MiniMind-V、多模态 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O、扩散语言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、线性模型（MiniMind-Linear），详见 Discussion。
* 项目所有核心算法代码均从 0 使用 PyTorch 原生实现，不依赖第三方库提供的高层抽象接口。
* 这不仅是一个大语言模型全阶段开源复现项目，也是一套面向 LLM 入门与实践的教程。
* 希望此项目能为更多人提供一个可复现、可理解、可扩展的起点，一起感受创造的乐趣，并推动更广泛 AI 社区的进步。

> 注：本项目基于 Apache 2.0 协议开源，完全免费。“2 小时” 指 SFT 阶段在单张 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 `1 epoch` 的实测耗时，“3 块钱” 指对应时段的 GPU 租用成本。

# 📌 项目介绍

大语言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出现，引发了全球范围内对 AI 的空前关注。无论是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 还是 Qwen，都以惊艳的效果让人真切感受到这场技术浪潮的冲击力。然而，动辄数百亿参数的模型规模，使得它们对个人设备而言不仅难以训练，甚至连部署都显得遥不可及。打开大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其内部运作机制，本应是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遗憾的是，绝大多数探索最终都止步于使用 LoRA 等技术对现有大模型做少量微调，学习一些新指令或特定任务。这更像是在教牛顿如何使用 21 世纪的智能手机——虽然有趣，却偏离了理解物理本质的初衷。

与此同时，第三方的大模型框架与工具库，如 `transformers` / `trl` / `peft` 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的接口。只需短短十几行代码，就可以完成“加载模型 + 加载数据集 + 推理 + 强化学习”的全流程训练。这种高效封装固然便利，却也在一定程度上把开发者与底层实现隔离开来，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心代码的机会。我认为 “用乐高自己拼出一架飞机，远比坐在头等舱里飞行更让人兴奋”，然而更现实的问题是，互联网上充斥着大量付费课程和营销内容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的讲解包装所谓的 AI 教程。正因如此，本项目的初衷就是尽可能降低 LLM 的学习门槛，让每个人都能从理解每一行代码开始，从 0 开始亲手训练一个极小的语言模型。是的，从**零开始训练**，而不是仅仅停留在**推理**层面。最低只需不到 3 块钱的服务器成本，就能亲身体验从 0 到 1 构建一个语言模型的全过程。

😊 一起感受创造的乐趣吧！

- 提供 Tokenizer 与分词器训练代码，支持 ` `、` `、` ` 等模板标记。

- 提供全阶段开源数据，覆盖收集、蒸馏、清洗与去重后的高质量数据集。
- 关键训练算法与核心模块均从 0 实现，不依赖第三方框架封装。
- 兼容 `transformers`、`trl`、`peft` 等主流框架，以及 `llama.cpp`、`vllm`、`ollama` 等常用推理引擎与 `Llama-Factory` 等训练框架。
- 支持单机单卡与单机多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）训练，支持 wandb / swanlab 可视化与动态启停训练。
- 支持在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方测评集上进行评测，并支持通过 YaRN 实现 RoPE 长文本外推。

# **🔥 Firecrawl**

**Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥** You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three.

- **Firecrawl Local.** Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost.
- **Firecrawl Cloud.** Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone.
- **Self-hosting.** Deploy the full Firecrawl server from `apps/api` with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure.

_Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)_

 
   
 

---

## Firecrawl Local

Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means `xcode-select --install` and on Debian or Ubuntu means `build-essential`.

```bash
cargo install firecrawl-local
```

If you don't have Rust, Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup.

```bash
npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev
```

Scrape a page and print its markdown.

```bash
firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown
```

Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page.

```bash
firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages
```

List every URL on a site.

```bash
firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev
```

Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning.

### Add it to your AI agent

`init` finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer.

```bash
firecrawl-local init
```

Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud.

### Run the Firecrawl API on localhost

`serve` answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key.

```bash
firecrawl-local serve
```

NGINX (pronounced "engine x" or "en-jin-eks") is the world's most popular Web Server, high performance Load Balancer, Reverse Proxy, API Gateway and Content Cache.

NGINX is free and open source software, distributed under the terms of a simplified 2-clause BSD-like license.

Enterprise distributions, commercial support and training are available from F5, Inc.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The goal of this README is to provide a basic, structured introduction to NGINX for novice users. Please refer to the full NGINX documentation for detailed information on installing, building, configuring, debugging, and more. These documentation pages also contain a more detailed Beginners Guide, How-Tos, Development guide, and a complete module and directive reference.

NGINX is installed software with binary packages available for all major operating systems and Linux distributions. See Tested OS and Platforms for a full list of compatible systems.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> While nearly all popular Linux-based operating systems are distributed with a community version of nginx, we highly advise installation and usage of official packages or sources from this repository. Doing so ensures that you're using the most recent release or source code, including the latest feature-set, fixes and security patches.

## Modules
NGINX is comprised of individual modules, each extending core functionality by providing additional, configurable features. See "Modules reference" at the bottom of nginx documentation for a complete list of official modules.

NGINX modules can be built and distributed as static or dynamic modules. Static modules are defined at build-time, compiled, and distributed in the resulting binaries. See Dynamic Modules for more information on how they work, as well as, how to obtain, install, and configure them.

```bash
nginx -V

items.summary: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference
items.content:
Open-source software toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models.
 

 
   Documentation   •   Blog   •   Key Features   •   Tutorials   •   Integrations   •   Benchmarks   •   Generative AI  
 

[](https://badge.fury.io/py/openvino)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/openvino-node)
[](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/openvino)
[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openvino)

[](https://pepy.tech/project/openvino)
[](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/openvino/files)
[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openvino)
  

- **Inference Optimization**: Boost deep learning performance in computer vision, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, natural language processing with large and small language models, and many other common tasks.
- **Flexible Model Support**: Use models trained with popular frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax. Directly integrate models built with transformers and diffusers from the Hugging Face Hub using Optimum Intel. Convert and deploy models without original frameworks.
- **Broad Platform Compatibility**: Reduce resource demands and efficiently deploy on a range of platforms from edge to cloud. OpenVINO™ supports inference on CPU (x86, ARM), GPU (Intel integrated & discrete GPU) and AI accelerators (Intel NPU).
- **Community and Ecosystem**: Join an active community contributing to the enhancement of deep learning performance across various domains.

Check out the OpenVINO Cheat Sheet and Key Features for a quick reference.

## Installation

Get your preferred distribution of OpenVINO or use this command for quick installation:

```sh
pip install -U openvino
```

### Verify Installation

After installation, you can verify OpenVINO is installed correctly by running:

```python
import openvino as ov
print(ov.__version__)
```

Check system requirements and supported devices for detailed information.

## Tutorials and Examples

OpenVINO Quickstart example will walk you through the basics of deploying your first model.

Learn how to optimize and deploy popular models with the OpenVINO Notebooks 📚:
- Create an LLM-powered Chatbot using OpenVINO
- YOLOv11 Optimization
- Text-to-Image Generation
- Multimodal assistant with LLaVa and OpenVINO
- Automatic speech recognition using Whisper and OpenVINO

Discover more examples in the OpenVINO Samples (Python & C++) and Notebooks (Python).

Here are easy-to-follow code examples demonstrating how to run PyTorch and TensorFlow model inference using OpenVINO:

**PyTorch Model**

```python
import openvino as ov
import torch
import torchvision

# load PyTorch model into memory
model = torch.hub.load("pytorch/vision", "shufflenet_v2_x1_0", weights="DEFAULT")

# convert the model into OpenVINO model
example = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)
ov_model = ov.convert_model(model, example_input=(example,))

# compile the model for CPU device
core = ov.Core()
compiled_model = core.compile_model(ov_model, 'CPU')

# infer the model on random data

items.title: 想换一台 MacBook，纠结 14 寸和 16 寸，求有实际使用经验的朋友聊聊
items.summary:
目前手里用的是一台 MacBook Air M2，24GB 内存、1TB 硬盘，平时主要就是办公、浏览网页、看看视频之类的。

一直以来对这台电脑都挺满意的，尤其是便携性。经常需要移动办公，有时候晚上躺在床上抱着电脑看看电视，也不会觉得重。14 寸左右的尺寸对我来说真的刚刚好，轻巧、方便，随时拿起来就能用。

不过之前买电脑的时候，主要考虑的就是日常办公和娱乐，并没有考虑过其他用途。

现在 AI 时代，自己也开始对本地 AI 模型产生兴趣，想折腾一些简单的本地模型，学习、测试一下，另外也会涉及一些代码编译、开发之类的工作。结果发现目前这台 Air 在这些场景下还是有点吃力，性能和散热都有些捉襟见肘。

所以最近有了换电脑的想法。

目前比较纠结的是尺寸问题。

个人还是非常喜欢 14 寸的尺寸，毕竟经常移动办公，也有躺床上使用的习惯，太大太重的话，便携性和使用体验都会打折扣。

但是网上看了不少评测，感觉 15 寸、16 寸的机器在散热、性能释放方面似乎会比 14 寸更有优势。不知道实际使用中差距到底有多大？尤其是长时间跑模型、编译代码这些场景，14 寸和 16 寸的体验会不会有明显区别？

目前个人比较关注 M3 Max 14 寸 MacBook Pro，感觉配置和尺寸似乎都比较符合自己的需求，但又担心 14 寸的散热和持续性能释放不如 16 寸。

想问问论坛里有没有实际使用过 14 寸和 16 寸 MacBook Pro 的朋友，特别是用来跑本地 AI 模型、开发、编译的朋友：

1. 14 寸和 16 寸在散热、持续性能释放方面，实际差距到底有多大？
2. 如果主要是跑一些中小型本地 AI 模型、日常开发和代码编译，14 寸 M3 Max 是否足够？
3. 16 寸除了屏幕大一些，性能和散热方面的优势是否真的值得牺牲便携性？
4. 如果经常移动办公，甚至偶尔躺床上抱着使用，16 寸会不会明显笨重？

目前个人还是更倾向于 14 寸，毕竟便携性对我来说真的很重要，但又不想买回来之后，因为散热或者性能释放的问题而后悔。

希望有实际使用经验的朋友分享一下，尤其是长期使用过这两个尺寸、跑过 AI 模型的朋友，想听听真实体验，而不只是参数和跑分。

先谢谢大家！

claude

**OpenAI SDK、Cherry Studio、Cline 等**：Base URL 填 `https://linyiapi.ai/v1`。

- 流式输出是真流式还是攒好了一次返回，并测出首 token 延迟。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Beijing-LINYIAI/api-relay-checker.git
cd api-relay-checker
python3 relay_check.py https://linyiapi.ai
```

items.summary:
我负责测 APP，以前 IOS 同事古法编程，开发完有 BUG 开完就改完了。
最近主管让他们用 AI 辅助开发，现在好了，BUG 量大量提升，最重要的是，出现了：
改完提出的 30 个 BUG，又出现了另外的 15 个 BUG，经典之改 A 出 B 问题。

但是我管控不了他们这么不负责任的做法。。。最终还是毒害到我身上。。。
现在测试工作时长差不多飙升了 1 倍

Feature Translation: The final struggles of a batch of near-death robotics companies Context: Xu Chuan (pseudonym) still holds out hope. Even though his former employer, a Guangdong-based robotics startup, owes him six months of salary, he has not yet pursued legal action (“The boss is actually a decent person,” he reasons). Plus, he hopes that the company can recover, choosing to ignore the fact that it has consistently failed to find stable commercial footing despite several pivots. Similar stories have unfolded throughout China’s robotics industry this year. In July, Yinghe Robotics [盈合机器人], once valued at USD$500 million, completed bankruptcy procedures; two months earlier, DeepBlue Robotics, a company backed by AI unicorn DeepBlueAI, also filed for bankruptcy. The winner of last week’s Around the Horn, a longform Huxiu article by Yuqin Yi — packed with interviews and data — details why so many Chinese robotics firms are barely hanging on to life. It ties together themes from two recent ChinAI issues: China’s venture capital ecosystem’s defiance of common sense, when it comes embodied AI ( ChinAI #381 ) China’s unsustainable embodied AI sector, built on murky guanxi relationships and limited technical capabilities ( ChinAI #372 ) Key Takeaways: DeepBlue Robotics and Yinghe Robotics constitute prominent failures, but they are part of a broader trend. From the article: “ An industry insider familiar with DeepBlue recalled that the company expanded rapidly over the past few years, extending its operations from smart retail into areas like autonomous driving and robotics. Its robotics division alone spanned various categories, including cleaning, delivery, disinfection, and gardening. ‘ Basically, whatever was hot, they would do ,’ the source noted .” After the breathless reports of initial deals, what actually transpired when it came to project fulfillment? In the case of DeepBlue, nothing. For instance, in 2021, the company boasted that South Korea’s LG Group had agreed to procure tens of thousands of intelligent disinfection robots. If we consider this exercise to be more akin to a prestige drama from the present-day TV landscape, we might already be on season 5. Let’s go back around the horn. This is our 28th roundup of articles on China’s AI ecosystem. For new readers, here’s how it works (see ChinAI #376 for the previous edition): I give short previews of ten articles that caught my eye during a scan through my usual sources (all published within the past week or so). The title for each preview links to the original article in Chinese. Readers vote on next week’s feature translation by replying to the email and/or commenting on the post with the number of your preferred article. *Extra weight goes to votes from those of you who support ChinAI through a paid subscription. items.content: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI - by Ethan Mollick One Useful Thing Subscribe Sign in Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI General, often expert, and sometimes jagged Ethan Mollick Nov 09, 2026 1,515 255 181 Share Before getting started, I wanted to thank my readers for making my new book, Co-Existence, a New York Times bestseller two weeks in a row. If you haven’t read it, you can get a copy here . I have had the chance to use the new Claude Fable 5.2 quite a bit before its public launch 1 , and it is very impressive, following on the already excellent Opus 5.5. AI has gotten so good, in fact, that it is worth asking if Anthropic’s newest models (and the inevitable competing models OpenAI and Google will soon release) cross the boundary into being an Artificial General Intelligence? AGI is a much-debated term with a lot of potential definitions. For this post, I’ll go with: “an AI as good as most human experts at most intellectual tasks you can do with a computer.” This explicitly excludes a lot of human work, including interacting with the physical world and other people, as well as most actual jobs, where “using a computer” is just one task among many. Still, even with these caveats, building a limited form of AGI has long been the goal of AI developers. So as not to keep you in suspense, I think the answer is that this is “almost” AGI, or what I have called Jagged AGI. Even within my limited definition, there are still important areas in many tasks where AI is jagged enough to fall well behind human capability. But the jaggedness is no longer about simple errors or hallucinations, which makes it harder to describe. So I want to try to do that in this post by showing you what Fable can do and where the gaps are. To get started I asked the new model: “I write OneUsefulThing among other stuff, I need you to create the most impressive thing I can share with people when you launch. It needs to be embeddable in a post and i can preface it however you like. it needs to have a visceral impact on people to show what you can do and the range of capabilities. It should grab them quickly. Be amazingly clever about this.” Fable asked me not to reveal anything until you had watched its video to the end. This was in one shot, with no feedback from me beyond the prompt. There is creativity here (including in the twist ending) and judgment and playfulness and cleverness. This is, I think, at the level of a human expert trying to make a movie with code alone, the sort of performance I would once have associated with AGI. The “G” in AGI Code and video creation have been areas where AI development has focused, so is Fable 5.2 really a General Intelligence? Looking back across the gap between these books is a good way to get a sense of AI progress. And, thanks to AI, I can describe this progress with some quite lovely charts. Making the charts is itself a good indicator of how far things have come. In the era of chatbots, the era of Co-Intelligence , I would have had to work back-and-forth with an AI in a chat window, guiding it through each new step. In the current era of agentic AI that I cover in Co-Existence , I delegated the work and let the AI handle it. In this case, I used Opus 5.5 in Claude Projects, which allows you to talk to a single “orchestrator” agent that then spins off additional agents as needed, giving them instructions and relaying information back to you. Getting the work done was straightforward. I gave the AI a couple sentences of suggestions and it did what would have taken me hours of work (all the research, all the graphing, all the layouts, all the images, all the citations…) in minutes. And since I didn’t have to do the work, I had the AI make many options for me. I picked some and gave handwavy reactions to others that would drive a human team mad (“make it better”). It even caught that I’d gotten the math wrong. I was going to call this post “28 months on the exponential.” Some examples of interacting with Claude to make the graphics for this post. Notice that it corrected me. “This is the worst AI you will ever use” I wrote this in my last book on AI, and it has continued to be literally true at every moment since. From early 2023 through early 2024, there was a single AI model that was undeniably the best in the world: GPT-4 from OpenAI. This was the AI model that most people remember from the first couple years of AI use, it was the one I thought about while writing Co-Intelligence , and it was the one that gave ChatGPT its status as the default AI for many people. Since then, twenty different AI models have held the lead at one time or another, all from Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI. Which company had the best AI model in the world. But the changing lead alone hides an even bigger change. A total of 180 AI models are now better than GPT-4 was at its release, many of which are open weights models, which anyone is free to use or modify. Nineteen of them can run on a modern smartphone. We are living in an exponential The data below draws on the METR Long Horizon Benchmark, which used to be the most famous chart in AI. items.content: The Dot and the Swarm - by Ethan Mollick - One Useful Thing One Useful Thing Subscribe Sign in The Dot and the Swarm Benefitting from the Bitter Lesson Ethan Mollick Oct 01, 2026 1,409 236 144 Share I generally think I have done a good job anticipating the direction and pace of AI over the few years I have been writing this Substack, but I think I recently got something fairly large wrong. In the last year I have been posting about how I suspected that humans would have to approach working with agents as a manager, deciding how to delegate work to agents and specifying how those agents should be organized. I thought that getting agents to work effectively as a group would take careful construction, akin to building a company, and that this would take time to figure out. Nope. I fell prey to The Bitter Lesson, the hard truth, learned over and over again, that things that we thought required elaborate human rules and thinking can be solved with the brute force of better machine learning systems and more AI. The Bitter Lesson is everywhere among AI startups and companies adopting AI. A huge amount of effort went into building elaborate computer systems to feed AIs the right information at the right time, but AI systems have learned to seek out information themselves. The same thing happened to prompting. People built elaborate templates and chains of prompts that walked the AI through a task one step at a time. Then newer models turned out to be better at planning the steps themselves, and, as our research shows , planning steps have much less value. The history of the Bitter Le— — you know what? I don’t really need to explain the Bitter Lesson, I asked Claude to do it in a music video. With one prompt, Fable wrote the lyrics and submitted it to Suno; Opus 5.5 did everything else using code alone without any image generation (How did Opus 5.5 pull this off? The Bitter Lesson tells you!). I gave no feedback at all. As somebody who teaches managers and has published research on management, I guess I believed that managing agents would be different. Humans have been working on management for a very long time without fully figuring it out. It seemed like the kind of thing that would need to be designed by people, at least for a while. It turns out that organizing work is just one more thing AI can learn to do. Which brings us to dots and Muse. items.content: Commitment issues (app edition) - by Ben Tossell Ben’s Bites Subscribe Sign in Commitment issues (app edition) It’s not me, it’s you Ben Tossell Nov 24, 2026 54 1 1 Share Last week, a mathematician spent six weeks with Claude and proved the Riemann hypothesis. A maths problem nobody had cracked since 1859. Then there’s me. I built a clock. P.s. The full interactive version of this post is here . Something in my tiny pea brain stops me working out What time is 10am PT in UK? without using super intelligence. I’m not proud of my chat history. It’s as bad as my calculator history. 200+65 is 265 btw. My clock lives in my menu bar. Type a time and a city, or drag it, and every city changes. presets for demo only It handles daylight savings too. Because of course the UK and US change their clocks on different weekends. You may be thinking ‘There’s a million clock apps that do this for free’. And you’re absolutely right. But I’ve got commitment issues. I’m always window shopping. Lots of apps are good enough but it feels like the grass is always greener. A lot of great tools come down to a few small features I really like. But they’re not making it for me. They’re making it for everyone. They need more users, so they add more features, and they put the price up. Or they’re free and get forgotten. It’s not me, it’s you. And I’m no better with AI models. Right now I’m using Gemini 4 Neon after turning my back on Google. A new model comes around and I pack my bags and move in. I obviously need the best to answer my very hard questions. The trouble with juggling multiple models at once is keeping track of them. Who am I neglecting? Who’s about to cut me off? Other apps I tried had more than I needed, so I made a stripped down version with just the things I care about. sliding usage is just used to show the menu icon syncing Screenshots are another one. I take a lot of full-page screenshots. Things I’ve built, to check them, or sites I like the look of, to ‘borrow’ from. So now I have an extension that does that. Browsers are a different beast. They’re a marriage. We spend a lot of time in them. So this relationship has been one of my biggest headaches. I’m sure I could build my own but it feels like a lot of work. I loved Arc, like many others. Then they got bought and ditched it. So I went back to Chrome. Then the people behind Arc came out with Dia, so I went crawling back to my ex, who’d had some work done. It was kinda the same but not quite. Then I dated someone literally named after both of my exes, Arc and Dia - Ardia. No red flags there. Then it got slow. So I stopped looking and just taught Chrome all my ex’s best moves: A way to ‘peek’ links - which shows you a mini window of the page you click Click to open a page in split view Vertical tabs (Chrome added this anyway) Ad blocking, no cookie banners And my biggest need - the tab switcher. I built my own extension + mac app that does all of that. Plus I can add in some extra niceties like defaultin

Nov 19, 2026 46 3 Share The other day my wife was chatting with AI. P.s. The full interactive version of this post is here . So let’s overlook the actual impossibilities and find out. Let’s be generous. Assume everyone types at world-record speed, 200 words a minute, non-stop. Everyone is happy to wait 10 minutes for a reply. items.content: Productiv-icky - by Ben Tossell - Ben's Bites Ben’s Bites Subscribe Sign in Productiv-icky Digging holes on the beach Ben Tossell Nov 17, 2026 79 4 2 Share productiv-icky (adj.) - the feeling of doing work you didn’t mean to do We have a problem. full interactive post is here We agree this is insane, right? Someone I don’t know sends me emails that I’m expected to reply to. I don’t know them. I don’t work for them. So I ignore them (well actually I send them to email jail). Nuh-uh, that’s not my work, buddy. But it’s different if it’s my super-intelligent, helpful agent friend… Yeses are easy. They’re quick. But every yes has a yes-tax. The hidden extra work you didn’t think of. The long tail of regret where you question why you ever said yes. Say I did reply to those emails, they’d send me stuff to read to show how great they are at their job and how much better I’d be. Then we’d organise a call (which would derail whichever day that call was on). Then we’d have follow-up items. Then a string of other crap I couldn’t care less about. I know what’s going to happen. I can smell it, it stinks. I’ve said yes and paid the tax many times before. Now I pay $200/mo for a super-intelligent, over-eager, needy little nerd to ping me incessantly about taking things off my plate. I feel bad for him. He wants to work. He’s gagging for it. Just. One. More. Task. Master. Plus, my little nerd has a gambling problem. Or rather, he feeds mine. Remember years ago sending tons of Slack messages to get the most out of your $20/mo plan? Nor me. Why? Because it’s dumb. But now we feel like we should use all our tokens before they run out. Why? Because everyone else is. We started measuring shovels instead of the hole. Someone’s needy little nerd booked their dentist, replied to their mum and launched a business whilst they were asleep. They’ve got an org chart. For nerds. With a Chief of Staff. You feel behind. Like way behind. So you grab a shovel and start digging. A little hole over there to triage your inbox, one here to draft your tweets, one to check on those. Then you spend your day checking the holes are being dug right. Before long, you’re surrounded by holes and a mountain of dirt you gotta do something with. Now as a man, holes are hardwired into my DNA. A few beers, a beach and a shovel, I’m digging a hole. I’d take pride in it. I’d make the best one, impressively round, deep enough to see sea water seep through the bottom. But I’d only dig one. There’s a whole beach but I chose this spot. Next time the needy little nerd pings you: do you really want another hole? Also, don’t dig big holes on the beach. They collapse.
